ov: The familiar orange fox of the northern hemisphere and the most widespread wild carnivore on Earth. A solitary hunter of small animals that has moved into farmland and cities.

why.ac: Mostly active at dusk and at night, though often seen by day where it isn’t disturbed.

rg: Across Europe, Asia, North America and North Africa. It was introduced to Australia in the 1830s and 1840s and is now an invasive predator there.
df: Small rodents and rabbits, birds, insects, fruit and berries, and scraps from bins in towns.
fx: In Australia it has been linked to the decline or extinction of several native mammals, including the desert rat-kangaroo.

_cf.tip: The Arctic fox is smaller than the red fox, with a rounder body and white winter coat.
The fennec is far smaller than a red fox, with much bigger ears.
